svg.title: An approved sprint reaches a PR
svg.desc: New full-lane sprint, normal premium path. The initial HTML pair uses its qualified one-reply transaction. There are no attended per-batch pauses; real hard gates still stop. This is a source-traced route, not a captured host run. Actual endpoint: An open PR and sprint receipt with current evidence, decisions and remaining work. The sprint never merges or discards the branch. Conditions and return paths remain in the companion reading view.

Manrope Variable, Segoe UI, Arial, sans-serif

svg.text: Review the pair → execute within scope → inspect the PR

svg.title: Review the whole sprint
svg.desc: command: /ca:sprint: select the work → skill: brainstorming: sprint definition → skill: writing-plans: linked draft → command: /ca:sprint: initial pair approval. Both exact artifact identities are approved and bound. A draft, a generic yes or an unobserved reply cannot begin execution.

path.title: define scope: The selected new sprint enters the definition phase.
draft pair: Planning may read this ready draft only through the initial sprint pair path.
review together: Present the complete pair and exact delegation terms before the host observes approval.

g.title: /ca:sprint: select the work. Resolve an existing exact-format pair before starting new work. This map follows a new HTML pair; existing Markdown retains its own contract.

g.title: brainstorming: sprint definition. Capture the outcome, exclusions, priorities and hard constraints. Consult recorded intent before asking for approval.

g.title: writing-plans: linked draft. For the initial pair, use the draft-for-pair path. Review criteria, tasks, tests, paths, dependencies and checkpoints together.

g.title: /ca:sprint: initial pair approval. The qualified adapter arms both definitions. Its exact reply names both artifacts and approve-only or delegate-methods. One observed reply commits approval and binding in a recoverable transaction.

path.title: eligible task: Select a fresh author for this bounded task.
test first: TDD happens inside the task, not after all authoring is done.
independent proof: The task caller obtains the separate review and fresh verification.

g.title: subagent-driven-development: select. The sprint hands the approved plan directly to the task engine rather than inserting executing-plans human checkpoints. Eligibility and current context tickets still constrain the task.

g.title: Scope-selected author. Dispatch the appropriate backend, frontend or infrastructure author with the task context. The author is not the reviewer who accepts its result.

g.title: tdd inside authoring. Derive obligations, demonstrate the intended RED failure, then satisfy the same assertion and the declared quality requirements.

g.title: Task engine: specification review and verification. Inspect specification compliance and run the plan verification afresh. A self-reported author pass cannot supply required host authority.

path.title: classify: The active caller retains responsibility for severity and scope.
no blocker: Only applicable current evidence permits acceptance.

g.title: Combined quality reviewers. Review the combined diff once the tasks have their required proof. Security, dependency and migration reviewers are path-selected rather than an unconditional roster.

path.title: current commit: The normal completion path reaches finalization.
reuse procedure: Run the existing procedure without invoking its entry again.
review before PR: Only the actual reviewer results support the final verdict.

g.title: commit-gate. Plan completion returns through the normal permission, selected-file and fresh-evidence gate. Recovery is not additional commit or publication authority.

g.title: finishing-a-development-branch. Sprint mode selects Open a PR instead of asking for attended terminal choices. Merge and discard are excluded.

g.title: /ca:pr procedure reused in place. The finisher executes the PR procedure here; the command is not re-invoked. Existing caller ownership prevents a routing loop.
